bull_case: Adobe is commercializing AI across creation, documents and enterprise workflows at large installed-base scale, turning disruption into multiple adjacent value pools.
bear_case: Adobe remains an incumbent responding to a cost/performance discontinuity created by external models; rapid usage does not yet prove superior AI unit economics or control of the new value chain.
thesis: Adobe shows real AI commercialization but does not yet satisfy a high disruptive-innovation score. AI-first ending ARR is >$650M and >150% y/y; Firefly ending ARR approached $300M at Q2 under a broader definition; creative freemium MAU exceeds 100M. Adoption is clearly accelerating, but Firefly-specific economics are unavailable. Adobe has multiple adjacent AI value pools, yet evidence does not establish that it defines the new AI value-chain standard.

evidence.claim: Q3 AI-first ending ARR exceeded $650M and grew >150% y/y.
Q2 Firefly ending ARR across Firefly App, credit packs and Firefly Enterprise was approaching $300M.
Creative freemium MAU crossed 100M and grew >70% y/y; Adobe reported >1B MAU across creativity/productivity.
AI commercialization spans at least creative generation, document productivity and enterprise customer-experience workflows.

counterevidence: Adobe did not originate the foundation-model cost curve and faces well-capitalized model/platform competitors.
Firefly-specific inference margin and contribution margin are not disclosed.
Three adjacent value pools are present, but evidence does not establish Adobe as the standard-setter for the new AI value chain.
unknowns: Whether Adobe or model/platform vendors capture the majority of incremental AI value.
falsifiers: AI-first ARR growth decelerates toward or below total ARR growth before achieving material scale.
AI MAU grows without corresponding paid ARR/cash conversion.
Core workflows shift to external model-native platforms that bypass Adobe.

key_kpis.name: AI-first ARR
key_kpis.threshold: sustain materially faster growth than total ARR

next_checks: Q4 AI-first ARR absolute value and composition.
Evidence of standard-setting/control in agentic creative or enterprise workflows.

subscores.rationale: Between 50 and 75: generative AI structurally changes creation/productivity economics, but Adobe is an incumbent responder and does not demonstrate a unique 10x cost curve.
Rapid ARR/MAU acceleration exceeds early adoption, but the 75 anchor requires economic confirmation; Firefly-specific unit economics are not disclosed.
Observable anchor: Adobe has at least two clearly monetized adjacent AI value pools and likely three, but lacks evidence that it defines the new value-chain standard required for 85.

uncertainties.rationale: AI is a structural cost/performance shift, but Adobe is primarily adapting to it rather than uniquely creating it.
ARR and MAU acceleration are verified; unit economics are not.
Multiple adjacent value pools are entered, but new value-chain standard control is unproven.
